The p text node is only punctuation/symbol characters (----=====++++ ...), so it does not express anything in human language; the expectation's exception applies even though #000 on #666 is only 3.66:1.

input#age (spinbutton) has an error indicator: span#error "Invalid value for age. Age must be at least 1." is exposed via aria-describedby on the Submit button. It is display:none, so no indicator describes the cause or fix in visible text; Expectation 2 fails.

aria-orientation is set on an audio element in the accessibility tree. It is not a global property; audio has no implicit role, and ARIA in HTML allows on audio only global attributes plus those of its allowed role application, which does not support aria-orientation. No expectation condition holds.

button is focusable (and carries a non-global ARIA attribute), so role=none is ignored by presentational roles conflict resolution and the semantic role is button. aria-pressed is a supported property of button, so the attribute is permitted.

img alt "nyhavn.jpeg" equals its src filename, so the rule applies. The img sits inside <a download href=...nyhavn.jpeg>, where the image's purpose is to identify the file being downloaded; the filename therefore serves an equivalent purpose to the non-text content.

The case is a bare <svg xmlns=...></svg> document, authored as an SVG (image/svg+xml) document. Its document element is svg, not an html element with content type text/html, so the rule does not apply.

The case is a bare <math></math> document, authored as a MathML (application/mathml+xml) document. Its document element is a math element, not an html element with content type text/html, so the rule does not apply.

div[role=menu] owns a group whose children are a menuitem and another div[role=group]. menu's required owned elements allow group only when the group itself owns only menuitem/menuitemradio/menuitemcheckbox; the nested group breaks that, so the menu fails.
div[role=list] owns, in the accessibility tree, a span[role=listitem] and a div[role=group]. The ARIA 1.2 required owned elements of list are listitem only; group is not permitted, so the list fails.

The only meta has content "0: https://w3.org"; ':' after the time digits is not ';', ',' or whitespace, so the shared declarative refresh steps abort and the content value is invalid. No meta meets the applicability, so inapplicable.

First meta content "0: https://w3.org" is invalid: after the digits the shared declarative refresh steps require ';', ',' or whitespace, and ':' aborts. The first valid refresh meta is content="5; https://w3.org", time 5, which is neither 0 nor over 72000.

The only meta has content "0: http://example.com"; the ':' following the time digits aborts the shared declarative refresh steps, so the content value is invalid and the meta does not meet applicability.

First meta content "0: https://w3.org" is invalid (':' after the digits aborts the shared declarative refresh steps). The first valid refresh meta is content="5; https://w3.org" with time 5, which is not 0, so the no-exception rule fails.

a[href] is focusable, so presentational roles conflict resolution ignores role=none and the element keeps the link role, included in the accessibility tree. Its only content is whitespace, so the accessible name is empty.

The canvas has nothing drawn (scripts off, no content), so it renders fully transparent; making it transparent changes no pixels, so it is not visible. Applicability requires a visible img, canvas or svg; none exists.

Both div[role=listitem] (explicit role, implicit role differs) are referenced by aria-owns on div[role=list]. aria-owns reparents them in the accessibility tree, so their parent there is the list, a required context role, despite the intervening navigation in the DOM.

h1 has role=none but also the global ARIA attribute aria-label, so presentational roles conflict resolution ignores none and the element remains a semantic heading in the accessibility tree. aria-label is empty and the only content is aria-hidden, so the accessible name is empty.
